# macos: capture selected settings as JSON with a CUE contract

## Motivation

Keep a readable, repeatable inventory of selected macOS settings in dotfiles,
so the workstation owner can inspect changes and build toward configuration as
code. The inventory must distinguish stored preferences from effective UI
behavior and desired configuration, including explicit gaps in coverage.

This is a bounded capture feature. Choosing a workstation management platform
remains separate research in [[DOT-144]] and [[DOT-396]].

## PoC

```sh
python3 config/macos/export.py
cue vet -c config/macos/settings.cue "config/macos/$(scutil --get LocalHostName).json" -d '#Snapshot'
git diff -- config/macos
```

An observation names its source and records either a stored value, an absent
key, or a read failure. Repeating capture with unchanged inputs produces the
same JSON. A missing key does not become a guessed default.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Selected macOS preferences can be captured without changing system settings or requiring sudo.
- [x] `settings.cue` describes known settings, their source mappings, types and valid observation states; the exporter and validation use the same catalog.
- [x] False and zero remain values; absent keys and failed reads remain distinct; unsupported values cannot silently disappear or pass as valid observations.
- [x] Output is deterministic for unchanged inputs; fatal collection or validation failure preserves an existing destination, and partial-capture behavior is explicit and distinguishable from usage errors.
- [x] A local snapshot passes validation, and reproducible checks cover malformed input, invalid states, read failures and output preservation.
- [x] The README explains commands, data flow, current coverage, evidence limits, blind spots, extension rules and the staged plan toward desired configuration and application.
- [x] Each host keeps its own snapshot, `config/macos/<LocalHostName>.json`, named the way `self-update` picks the host Brewfile, so hosts do not overwrite each other.

Acceptance is local. The snapshot does not establish effective UI behavior or
compatibility with other machines or macOS releases.

## Out of scope

Applying settings; changing permissions or management profiles; claiming full
System Settings coverage; introducing Nix or Ansible; publishing issues,
comments or branches to GitHub; committing changes. New backends and a desired
configuration model belong to later work.
